sentences.en: For more than 500 days, coal miners in rural Alabama have been on strike in one of the longest work stoppages in American history.
sentences.zh: 在阿拉巴马州的农村，煤矿工人们已经罢工超过500天，这是美国历史上持续时间最长的工作停摆之一。

sentences.en: The difference between us and the people who are keeping us out here, who don't want to give us a free contract, is want.
sentences.zh: 我们和那些把我们拒之门外、不愿给我们一份公平合同的人之间的区别，就在于“意愿”二字。

sentences.en: We're the ones that gave them a right to be billionaires.
sentences.zh: 是我们让他们有了成为亿万富翁的资本。

sentences.en: But as the strike drags on, the miners are discovering that neither political party is willing to fight for them.
sentences.zh: 但随着罢工的拖延，矿工们发现，没有任何一个政党愿意为他们而战。

sentences.en: I could see some light.
sentences.zh: 我能看到一点曙光了。

sentences.en: For the first time, I could see some light.
sentences.zh: 这是我第一次看到曙光。

sentences.en: Today, my colleague Michael Corkery has the story of one coal miner and how the strike has transformed his view of American politics.
sentences.zh: 今天，我的同事迈克尔·科克里将讲述一位煤矿工人的故事，以及这场罢工如何改变了他对美国政治的看法。

sentences.en: You have proven once again that you belong to the fightingest, toughest, longstanding union in the history of man, to united mine workers of America.
sentences.zh: 你们再次证明了你们属于美国矿工联合会，这是人类历史上最顽强、最坚韧、历史最悠久的工会。

sentences.en: And I am so proud of you.
sentences.zh: 我为你们感到无比自豪。

sentences.en: It's Monday, August 22nd.
sentences.zh: 今天是8月22日，星期一。

sentences.en: Michael, tell me about this strike.
sentences.zh: 迈克尔，跟我说说这场罢工吧。

sentences.en: This strike is arguably the biggest labor story in the country, and yet it's getting very little attention.
sentences.zh: 这场罢工可以说是全国最大的劳工事件，但却几乎没有得到什么关注。

sentences.en: Just to give you a sense of the scale, there's about 900 coal miners who walked off the job in April 2021, and they haven't been back since.
sentences.zh: 为了让你了解规模，大约有900名煤矿工人在2021年4月停工，从那以后就再没回去过。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: It's rare that people are willing in this day and age to leave their job and take a risk and go on strike.
sentences.zh: 在当今这个时代，人们愿意离开工作岗位去冒险罢工，这很罕见。

sentences.en: But to go on strike for more than a year, I mean more than 500 days, that's just unheard of.
sentences.zh: 但罢工超过一年，也就是超过500天，这简直闻所未闻。

sentences.en: So I decided to go down there and talk to the workers and try to understand exactly what had made them take to the picket lines and to stay out there for so long.
sentences.zh: 所以我决定去那里和工人们谈谈，试图弄清楚到底是什么让他们走上纠察线，并坚持了这么久。

sentences.en: So who did you end up speaking with in Alabama at this strike?
sentences.zh: 那么你在阿拉巴马州的这场罢工中最终采访了谁？

sentences.en: This company isn't treating us fairly.
sentences.zh: 这家公司对待我们不公平。

sentences.en: That's the bottom line.
sentences.zh: 这就是问题的关键。

sentences.en: That's all you can say.
sentences.zh: 这就是你所能说的全部。

sentences.en: I spoke to coal miners of every type.
sentences.zh: 我采访了各种各样的煤矿工人。

sentences.en: Grandfathers, my father retired from the union, my uncle was retired from the union.
sentences.zh: 祖父辈的，我父亲从工会退休了，我叔叔也从工会退休了。

sentences.en: Miners that had been there for generations.
sentences.zh: 几代人都在那里工作的矿工。

sentences.en: Miners of different ages, races, backgrounds.
sentences.zh: 不同年龄、种族和背景的矿工。

sentences.en: I lost about $20,000 a year on just my W-2 alone.
sentences.zh: 仅我的W-2工资表上，我一年就损失了大约2万美元。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: That's $20,000 a year.
sentences.zh: 那可是一年2万美元。

sentences.en: And they all had different stories to tell, but many things in common, which was their commitment to staying on strike until they felt they were going to get a fair deal.
sentences.zh: 他们每个人都有不同的故事，但有很多共同点，那就是他们承诺在获得公平协议之前绝不停止罢工。

sentences.en: We gave up some things and water for us to get them back where they're supposed to be.
sentences.zh: 我们为了让他们回到正轨而做出了一些让步。

sentences.en: And now it's time for them to give back.
sentences.zh: 现在是他们回报的时候了。

sentences.en: I wish they would spend one week underground with us.
sentences.zh: 我真希望他们能和我们一起在地下待上一周。

sentences.en: And I think it wouldn't take two days of that one week for them to understand what bargaining in good faith should be.
sentences.zh: 我想不用两天，他们就能明白什么才是真正的诚意谈判。

sentences.en: We're definitely going to cross the line and go back to work.
sentences.zh: 我们肯定会跨过纠察线回去工作的。

sentences.en: We'll stay in the fight.
sentences.zh: 我们会继续战斗。

sentences.en: The day is coming.
sentences.zh: 那一天终会到来。

sentences.en: We're going to be back in that coal mine.
sentences.zh: 我们会回到那个煤矿的。

sentences.en: And we're going to be getting what we're supposed to have.
sentences.zh: 我们会得到我们应得的一切。

sentences.en: So that's what this is all about.
sentences.zh: 这就是这场罢工的全部意义所在。

sentences.en: And one of the people that I ended up spending a lot of time with was a coal mine worker named Braxton Wright.
sentences.zh: 我花了很多时间相处的人之一，是一位名叫布拉克斯顿·赖特的煤矿工人。

sentences.en: Oh, yeah.
sentences.zh: 哦，好的。

sentences.en: You want to ride around?
sentences.zh: 你想开车转转吗？

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 好啊，好啊。

sentences.en: We can take my truck.
sentences.zh: 我们可以开我的卡车。

sentences.en: Oh, great.
sentences.zh: 哦，太棒了。

sentences.en: I know I can tell you.
sentences.zh: 我知道我可以告诉你。

sentences.en: Yeah, I can tell you.
sentences.zh: 是的，我可以告诉你。

sentences.en: So Braxton's 39 years old.
sentences.zh: 布拉克斯顿今年39岁。

sentences.en: He grew up in this part of central Alabama, and he has settled and raised a family here.
sentences.zh: 他在阿拉巴马州中部长大，并在这里安家落户，养育了家庭。

sentences.en: And when I was in Alabama, he took me on a tour of where he lives.
sentences.zh: 当我在阿拉巴马州时，他带我参观了他居住的地方。

sentences.en: Does that help you quit the Indian?
sentences.zh: 那能帮你戒掉那个吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Do you have a flavor that you like?
sentences.zh: 你有喜欢的口味吗？

sentences.en: This one's called Melon Time.
sentences.zh: 这个叫“瓜之时光”。

sentences.en: Melon Time.
sentences.zh: “瓜之时光”。

sentences.en: I don't know what kind of melon it is, but it actually tastes pretty decent.
sentences.zh: 我不知道是什么瓜，但味道还挺不错的。

sentences.en: And it don't make me stink.
sentences.zh: 而且它不会让我有异味。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Braxton's been a miner for many, many years.
sentences.zh: 布拉克斯顿当矿工已经很多很多年了。

sentences.en: And his experience at the mine and just growing up in that part of Alabama really helped me understand what this fight at the mine, what this strike was really all about.
sentences.zh: 他在矿上的经历以及在阿拉巴马州那部分的成长过程，真的让我明白了这场矿山斗争，这场罢工的真正意义。

sentences.en: This seam is this, it's a coal seam that I guess this is juSt...
sentences.zh: 这个煤层是，我想这只是……

sentences.en: Yeah, Blue Creek coal seam is what we mine.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们开采的是蓝溪煤层。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But Blue Creek is supposed to be one of the best coal, or I guess we're really like the second best coal in the world.
sentences.zh: 但蓝溪被认为是最好的煤炭之一，或者我想我们其实是世界第二好的煤炭。

sentences.en: We're about 40 minutes away from Birmingham, which is a few towns away from the coal mine where Braxton works.
sentences.zh: 我们距离伯明翰大约40分钟路程，离布拉克斯顿工作的煤矿有几个镇的距离。

sentences.en: One of the coal companies back then was called Roden Coal, R-O-D-E-N.
sentences.zh: 当时其中一家煤炭公司叫罗登煤炭公司，R-O-D-E-N。

sentences.en: Every once in a while, you type in Roden Coal Company, it pulls up some pictures, and a lot of the pictures are from West Washington.
sentences.zh: 偶尔你输入“罗登煤炭公司”，它会跳出一些照片，很多照片都是来自西华盛顿的。

sentences.en: And all these towns around here spring up because of coal.
sentences.zh: 这周围所有的城镇都是因为煤炭而兴起的。

sentences.en: They were basically extensions of the coal companies, as Braxton later explained.
sentences.zh: 正如布拉克斯顿后来解释的那样，它们基本上是煤炭公司的延伸。

sentences.en: The town I live in, West Blockton, is actually a coal mining town.
sentences.zh: 我住的镇子，西布洛克顿，实际上就是一个煤矿小镇。

sentences.en: It got its name from, they claimed they found a block of coal that weighed a ton, so they named it Blockton.
sentences.zh: 它的名字由来是，他们声称发现了一块重达一吨的煤块，所以就把它命名为布洛克顿。

sentences.en: And then when Blockton burned down, they moved it just west of Blockton, so then it became West Blockton.
sentences.zh: 后来布洛克顿被烧毁了，他们就搬到了布洛克顿的西边，于是就变成了西布洛克顿。

sentences.en: And so, like many other people in his community, a couple of years after he graduates high school, Braxton entered the coal industry.
sentences.zh: 所以，像社区里的许多其他人一样，布拉克斯顿在高中毕业几年后就进入了煤炭行业。

sentences.en: When I went to the coal mines, they started me out at $18 an hour, and I was working 48 hours a week.
sentences.zh: 当我进入煤矿时，他们起薪是每小时18美元，我每周工作48小时。

sentences.en: And a lot of the times, I could work up to 60 hours if I wanted to.
sentences.zh: 很多时候，如果我想的话，我可以工作到60个小时。

sentences.en: You know, so I was 21 years old, and I went from making probably $33,000, $34,000 a year to making like $60,000 a year, you know, with the overtime.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我当时21岁，我的年收入从大约3.3万到3.4万美元，增加到了大约6万美元，你知道，加上加班费。

sentences.en: So, that's a pretty good job for, you know, for a guy your age and, you know, rural Alabama.
sentences.zh: 所以，对于你这个年纪的人，在阿拉巴马州的农村，那是一份相当不错的工作。

sentences.en: Yeah, it is.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实。

sentences.en: I mean, yeah.
sentences.zh: 我是说，是的。

sentences.en: It's 2005, he is at this coal mining company called Jim Walter Resources.
sentences.zh: 那是2005年，他在一家叫吉姆·沃尔特资源公司的煤矿公司工作。

sentences.en: When me and my wife got married is when I decided I wanted a career instead of, you know, I guess she settled me down, you know.
sentences.zh: 我和我妻子结婚时，我决定要一份职业，而不是，我想是她让我安定了下来。

sentences.en: I was running wild until I met her.
sentences.zh: 在遇到她之前，我一直过得很狂野。

sentences.en: That's when I decided I wanted to make a full career out of it, and that's when I started working even harder to try to, you know, move up in the company.
sentences.zh: 就在那时，我决定以此为终身职业，于是我开始更加努力地工作，试图在公司里晋升。

sentences.en: And so, Braxton sees himself spending his life in this company making a great living.
sentences.zh: 所以，布拉克斯顿把自己的一生都投入到了这家公司，过着优渥的生活。

sentences.en: And what is the state of the mining industry when he enters it in 2005?
sentences.zh: 那么当他在2005年进入矿业时，这个行业的状况如何？

sentences.en: Well, coal is in decline.
sentences.zh: 嗯，煤炭行业正在衰退。

sentences.en: The United States is no longer using it as its primary energy source and is transitioning to greener energy sources.
sentences.zh: 美国不再将其作为主要能源，并正在向更绿色的能源转型。

sentences.en: Because Braxton's coal mine produces coal, not for energy, but for steel making.
sentences.zh: 因为布拉克斯顿的煤矿生产的煤炭不是为了能源，而是为了炼钢。

sentences.en: And the American steel industry at that time is also in decline because much of it's being manufactured in China.
sentences.zh: 而当时的美国钢铁工业也处于衰退之中，因为大部分产品都是在中国制造的。

sentences.en: So, overall, the industry is troubled when he starts.
sentences.zh: 所以，总体而言，在他入行时，这个行业正处于困境。

sentences.en: And yet, he's still being paid very, very well and making for people in central Alabama an enormous amount of money.
sentences.zh: 然而，他的薪水依然非常非常高，对于阿拉巴马州中部的人来说，这是一笔巨款。

sentences.en: And the reason for that is pretty simple.
sentences.zh: 原因很简单。

sentences.en: In Washington, the coal operators and the miners' chiefs, led by John L.
sentences.zh: 在华盛顿，煤炭运营商和以约翰·L·刘易斯为首的矿工领袖们会面签署协议，结束了煤矿区九个月的动荡。

sentences.en: Lewis, meet to sign a contract, ending nine months' turmoil in the coal fields.
sentences.zh: 煤矿工人们属于一个极其强大的工会。

sentences.en: The coal miners are part of an extremely powerful union.
sentences.zh: 美国矿工联合会，历史上最古老、最富传奇色彩的工会之一。

sentences.en: The United Mine Workers of America, one of the oldest, most storied labor unions in history.
sentences.zh: 美国矿工联合会再次完成了不可能的任务。

sentences.en: The United Mine Workers of America has again accomplished the impossible.
sentences.zh: 他们再次在面对工会或工人自愿组织所遭遇的最强大的集中反对势力时，谈判达成了一项协议。

sentences.en: They have again negotiated an agreement against the greatest concentrated opposition that ever faced a labor union or a voluntary association of workmen.
sentences.zh: 而且他们相当激进。

sentences.en: And they are quite militant.
sentences.zh: 他们从不退缩。

sentences.en: They don't back down.
sentences.zh: 因此，随着时间的推移，他们能够为工人们争取到非常高的工资和良好的福利。

sentences.en: And as a result of that, they've been able to gain very high wages and good benefits for their workers over time.
sentences.zh: 我们取得了新的成果。

sentences.en: We have made new gains.
sentences.zh: 我们造福了所有劳动者。

sentences.en: We have benefited all labor.
sentences.zh: 我们造福了所有生活在我们旗帜下的公民。

sentences.en: And we have benefited all citizens who live under our flag.
sentences.zh: 你知道，煤矿工作通常只需要高中学历，却能提供相当舒适的中产阶级生活。

sentences.en: You know, coal mining, which you often do with only a high school education, offers quite a comfortable middle-class life.
sentences.zh: 许多矿工拥有自己的房子、多辆汽车，还能送孩子上大学。

sentences.en: Many miners own their homes, multiple cars, send their kids to college.
sentences.zh: 这很大程度上要归功于矿工工会。

sentences.en: And a lot of that is attributed to the mine workers' union.
sentences.zh: 那么布拉克斯顿与工会的关系如何？

sentences.en: And what is Braxton's relationship to the union?
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，他刚开始工作时并不是工会成员。

sentences.en: So, interestingly, when he started, he was not a member of the union.
sentences.zh: 从我开始工作起，我就一直喜欢和那些老工会成员一起工作。

sentences.en: From the time I started, I always liked working with the older union guys.
sentences.zh: 但他对工会工人有着极大的钦佩，钦佩他们的思维方式，他们对工作的看法，以及他们对自身所拥有的权力和影响力的看法。

sentences.en: But he had enormous admiration for the union workers and how they thought and how they thought about their jobs and how they thought about the power and influence they had.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我从那一代建立并开启这些煤矿的人身上学到了很多。

sentences.en: You know, I learned so much from the generation that built and started those coal mines.
sentences.zh: 我实际上和他们一起工作了很多年。

sentences.en: I actually got to work with for years.
sentences.zh: 我交了很多很好的朋友，也学到了很多，你知道，就是坐着听那些老手们讲故事。

sentences.en: And I made a lot of really good friends and I learned a lot just, you know, sitting around listening to the stories that some of the, you know, the old hands would tell.
sentences.zh: 我想那可能是我工作中我最喜欢的部分，就是听他们讲故事，从他们那里学习关于煤矿的事情。

sentences.en: And I think that was probably my favorite part of the job was just listening to them and learning, you know, stuff about the coal mines from them.
sentences.zh: 最终他成为了那个工会的成员。

sentences.en: And eventually he becomes a member of that union.
sentences.zh: 这件事发生的方式有点不同寻常，但考虑到当时煤炭行业发生的事情，也不足为奇。

sentences.en: It happened in a way that was a bit unusual, but not unexpected given what was happening in the coal industry at the time.
sentences.zh: 解释一下。

sentences.en: Explain that.
sentences.zh: 你是什么意思？

sentences.en: What do you mean?
sentences.zh: 嗯，2015年，他工作的煤矿公司吉姆·沃尔特资源公司面临着巨大的财务问题。

sentences.en: Well, in 2015, the coal mining company he's working for, Jim Walter Resources, it's facing a ton of financial probleMs.
sentences.zh: 它背负着沉重的债务，煤价暴跌，他们正在裁员，包括布拉克斯顿在内。

sentences.en: It's weighed down with debt, the price of coal had crashed, and they were laying off people, including Braxton.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我从基层做起，多年来我努力工作，证明了我的知识和独立管理工厂的能力。

sentences.en: You know, I'd started off in a low position and I had worked so hard for so many years to prove my knowledge and my ability to run a plant on my own.
sentences.zh: 你知道，做决定、做维护，做所有这些其他事情。

sentences.en: You know, make decisions, do maintenance, do all this other stuff.
sentences.zh: 然后突然之间他们说，嘿，我们不再需要你了。

sentences.en: And then all of a sudden to say, you know, hey, we don't need you anymore.
sentences.zh: 那部分对我来说真的很艰难。

sentences.en: That part was really tough on me.
sentences.zh: 我可能受到的打击最大，你知道，我辛辛苦苦才爬到这个位置，结果他们就像对待垃圾一样把我解雇了。

sentences.en: I took that probably the hardest of all, you know, that I had worked so hard to build up to my position and then they just let me go like I was nothing.
sentences.zh: 大约一年后，正如这些公司通常做的那样，吉姆·沃尔特资源公司进行了重组，换了个新名字。

sentences.en: And then about a year later, as these companies tend to do, Jim Walter Resources reorganizes itself, gets a new name.
sentences.zh: 它叫勇士冶金煤公司，又雇回了数百名矿工。

sentences.en: It's called Warrior Met Coal, and it hires hundreds of miners back.
sentences.zh: 布拉克斯顿就是其中之一。

sentences.en: Braxton's one of them.
sentences.zh: 这一次，他被聘为工会职位。

sentences.en: And this time he's hired into a union job.
sentences.zh: 那是我感到自豪的时刻，你知道，当你成为一名工会煤矿工人时。

sentences.en: It was a proud moment for me, you know, when you were a union coal miner.
sentences.zh: 你知道，很多人都很敬仰工会煤矿工人。

sentences.en: You know, a lot of people kind of looked up to the union coal miners.
sentences.zh: 这是一种——他们有着在需要时把事情办成的历史。

sentences.en: It was a – they'd had a history of, you know, getting things done when it needed to be done.
sentences.zh: 好的，现在他是这个工会的成员了，正如你所说，他对此深感钦佩。

sentences.en: Okay, so now he's a member of this union, which, as you've said, he deeply admired.
sentences.zh: 那么结果对他来说有什么改变吗？

sentences.en: So how do things change for him as a result?
sentences.zh: 嗯，即使从一开始，这家新重组的公司，情况也不如从前了。

sentences.en: Well, even from the outset, this newly organized company, things are not as good as they used to be.
sentences.zh: 为了让公司走出破产困境，工会被迫同意接受非常大幅度的工资削减和福利削减。

sentences.en: In order for the company to come out of bankruptcy, the union was forced to agree to take very significant wage cuts and cuts to their benefits.
sentences.zh: 但当时他们认为，而且工会领袖们说，他们曾明确被这家煤炭公司告知，一旦公司经营好转并开始盈利，

sentences.en: But then they assumed, and the union leaders say they were told explicitly by this coal company that once the company was doing better and had started turning a profit,
sentences.zh: 一切就会恢复原样。

sentences.en: their old wages and benefits would be restored.
sentences.zh: 他们以前的工资和福利待遇会得到恢复。

sentences.en: I started in April of 2016.
sentences.zh: 我是2016年4月开始在那儿工作的。

sentences.en: I guess that's when we started realizing that this company had made a major change.
sentences.zh: 我想就是从那时起，我们开始意识到这家公司发生了重大变化。

sentences.en: But it quickly became apparent that the company was not going to do that.
sentences.zh: 但很快大家就看出来，公司根本没打算那么做。

sentences.en: And Braxton says they knew this in part because the working conditions at the mine were much worse than before the bankruptcy.
sentences.zh: 布拉克斯顿说，他们之所以知道这一点，部分原因是矿井的工作条件比破产前还要糟糕得多。

sentences.en: We worked with skeleton crews.
sentences.zh: 我们当时是在精简人员的情况下工作的。

sentences.en: I mean, really, before the bankruptcy, we had 46 union guys.
sentences.zh: 我是说，真的，破产前我们有46名工会成员。

sentences.en: And then after the bankruptcy and we started back, we had 21 union guys.
sentences.zh: 破产重组后我们复工时，工会成员只剩下21个了。

sentences.en: So we were doing twice the work, you know, with less people.
sentences.zh: 所以我们是用更少的人干了两倍的活，你懂的。

sentences.en: So, you know, that was a big change.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，那是一个巨大的变化。

sentences.en: Now, the company disputes that, saying conditions were safe and legitimate.
sentences.zh: 现在，公司对此表示异议，称当时的工作条件是安全且合规的。

sentences.en: But the union and Braxton aren't happy with the way things are going.
sentences.zh: 但工会和布拉克斯顿对现状并不满意。

sentences.en: And this is all happening against the backdrop of the 2016 presidential election.
sentences.zh: 而这一切都发生在2016年总统大选的背景之下。

sentences.en: So you've come back to the mind, you're now a member of a union.
sentences.zh: 所以你回到了矿上，现在你成了工会的一员。

sentences.en: And this is 2016.
sentences.zh: 当时是2016年。

sentences.en: Nationally, coal mining becomes an issue in the presidential election between Hillary Clinton and Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 在全国范围内，煤矿开采成了希拉里·克林顿和唐纳德·特朗普之间总统竞选的一个议题。

sentences.en: Were you paying attention to that?
sentences.zh: 你有关注这件事吗？

sentences.en: And if so, what was your thinking at the time?
sentences.zh: 如果有的话，你当时是怎么想的？

sentences.en: Yeah, I was.
sentences.zh: 是的，我有关注。

sentences.en: You know, you know, I know historically, you know, the Democrats has always supported, you know, unions, but they're not necessarily coal miners.
sentences.zh: 你知道，从历史上看，民主党一直支持工会，但他们未必支持煤矿工人。

sentences.en: So for many decades, the coal mining union and Democrats went hand in hand.
sentences.zh: 所以几十年来，煤矿工会和民主党一直是紧密相连的。

sentences.en: The UMWA, the United Mine Workers of America, has been solidly democratic.
sentences.zh: 美国矿工联合会（UMWA）一直坚定地支持民主党。

sentences.en: In the 1930s, that union was the single largest contributor, the Democratic Party.
sentences.zh: 在20世纪30年代，该工会是民主党最大的单一捐款方。

sentences.en: Well, so, yeah, for a very long time, if you were a coal miner, you voted Democratic.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以，是的，在很长一段时间里，如果你是煤矿工人，你就会投票给民主党。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: I'm the only candidate which has a policy about how to bring economic opportunity using clean, renewable energy as the key into coal country.
sentences.zh: 我是唯一一位有政策主张的候选人，该政策旨在利用清洁、可再生能源作为关键，为煤炭产区带来经济机遇。

sentences.en: Of course, that has changed because for the Democratic Party, a big issue is climate change.
sentences.zh: 当然，情况已经变了，因为对于民主党来说，气候变化是一个重大议题。

sentences.en: And efforts to combat climate change and coal are not compatible.
sentences.zh: 而应对气候变化的努力与煤炭行业是不兼容的。

sentences.en: Because we're going to put a lot of coal miners and coal companies out of business.
sentences.zh: 因为我们要让很多煤矿工人和煤炭公司失业。

sentences.en: Right, Tim?
sentences.zh: 对吧，蒂姆？

sentences.en: And we're going to make it clear that we don't want to forget those people.
sentences.zh: 我们要明确表示，我们不会忘记那些人。

sentences.en: Those people labored in those mines for generations.
sentences.zh: 那些人世世代代在矿井里辛勤劳作。

sentences.en: So by 2016, confirming the union's worst fears were these statements made by Hillary Clinton.
sentences.zh: 所以到了2016年，希拉里·克林顿的这些言论证实了工会最担心的事。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: Hillary Clinton later said she was misquoted, quoted out of context.
sentences.zh: 希拉里·克林顿后来表示，她的话被引用错了，断章取义了。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, personally, I felt like, you know, if she had become president, that we'd, you know, we wouldn't have coal mines anymore.
sentences.zh: 是的，我是说，我个人觉得，如果她当选总统，我们可能就不会再有煤矿了。

sentences.en: You know, and I think a lot of people thought the same thing.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我想很多人也是这么想的。

sentences.en: But it really seemed to confirm what the coal miners had been feeling, which is that they can't count on the Democrats as their party any longer.
sentences.zh: 但这确实似乎证实了煤矿工人们一直以来的感受，那就是他们再也不能把民主党当作自己的政党了。

sentences.en: Meanwhile.
sentences.zh: 与此同时。

sentences.en: Coal is coming back.
sentences.zh: 煤炭行业正在复苏。

sentences.en: Clean coal is coming back.
sentences.zh: 清洁煤正在复苏。
百分之百。

sentences.en: On the other side of the aisle, Donald Trump seizes on this moment.
sentences.zh: 在政坛的另一边，唐纳德·特朗普抓住了这个时机。

sentences.en: She wants the mines closed and she will never let them work again.
sentences.zh: 她想关闭矿井，永远不让你们再工作了。

sentences.en: And uses that to become the champion of the aggrieved coal miner.
sentences.zh: 并利用这一点成为了受委屈的煤矿工人的捍卫者。

sentences.en: Let me tell you, they're going to start to work again.
sentences.zh: 让我告诉你们，他们会重新开始工作的。

sentences.en: Believe me.
sentences.zh: 相信我。

sentences.en: You're going to be proud again to be miners.
sentences.zh: 你们会再次为身为矿工而感到自豪。

sentences.en: And makes big promises that he's going to save their jobs, save the industry, bring coal back.
sentences.zh: 他做出了宏大的承诺，说他会保住他们的工作，拯救这个行业，让煤炭业重现辉煌。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: We thought, you know, hey, this is a businessman, you know, not a politician.
sentences.zh: 我们当时想，嘿，这是一个商人，不是政客。

sentences.en: You know, maybe he will, you know, look out for the workers and not just the interest of politicians, you know.
sentences.zh: 也许他会为工人着想，而不仅仅是考虑政客的利益。

sentences.en: Did you believe him back then that he would indeed save coal?
sentences.zh: 你当时相信他真的能拯救煤炭行业吗？

sentences.en: Yes, yes, I did.
sentences.zh: 是的，是的，我信了。

sentences.en: I mean, us being union coal miners, you know, it's kind of like, you know, the Republicans don't want us because we're union and the Democrats don't want us because we run coal,
sentences.zh: 我是说，作为工会煤矿工人，共和党不想要我们，因为我们是工会成员；民主党不想要我们，因为我们从事煤炭行业，

sentences.en: you know.
sentences.zh: 你懂的。

sentences.en: So we've always been in kind of a hard spot.
sentences.zh: 所以我们一直处于一种艰难的境地。

sentences.en: But, you know, then all of a sudden Trump comes in and says he's going to save coal mines.
sentences.zh: 但是，突然间特朗普来了，说他要拯救煤矿。

sentences.en: We just took it to heart that somebody, hey, somebody, you know, is going to speak up for the coal miners, you know.
sentences.zh: 我们真心觉得，终于有人要为煤矿工人说话了。

sentences.en: But Trump couldn't change the economics of coal and no matter how many regulations he rolled back, coal was in a death spiral and their industry and its fortunes did not improve.
sentences.zh: 但特朗普无法改变煤炭的经济规律，无论他废除了多少法规，煤炭行业都处于死亡螺旋之中，他们的行业及其命运并没有好转。

sentences.en: And meanwhile, at this reorganized company, 2021 comes along and it's coming up to a time to, you know, for the contract.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，在这家重组后的公司，时间到了2021年，合同续签的时间快到了。

sentences.en: Five years have passed and they remembered this company told them that when the next contract came around, they would be made whole and the things that they had given up,
sentences.zh: 五年过去了，他们还记得这家公司曾告诉他们，当下一份合同到来时，他们会得到补偿，他们放弃的东西，

sentences.en: they would get back again.
sentences.zh: 他们会重新拿回来。

sentences.en: Now, the company disputes that and has put out statements to the effect that they made no such promises, but that's not how the union remembers it.
sentences.zh: 现在，公司对此表示异议，并发表声明称他们从未做出过此类承诺，但工会记忆中的情况并非如此。

sentences.en: And they started to negotiate a new contract.
sentences.zh: 于是他们开始协商一份新合同。

sentences.en: And the company, you know, has not even put forth an effort, you know, of negotiating.
sentences.zh: 而公司甚至连谈判的努力都没有付出。

sentences.en: So, you know, a coal miner has always kind of been a respected, you know, worker.
sentences.zh: 所以，煤矿工人一直以来都是受人尊敬的劳动者。

sentences.en: But we've always had pride in our work and it got to the point to where we had no respect in the company.
sentences.zh: 我们一直为自己的工作感到自豪，但现在却到了我们在公司那里得不到任何尊重的地步。

sentences.en: But in the negotiations, the company was not getting back to where they were.
sentences.zh: 但在谈判中，公司并没有回到他们当初承诺的状态。

sentences.en: So, you know, we we worked through 2020, you know, through coronavirus.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们在2020年，在新冠疫情期间，依然坚持工作。

sentences.en: And on top of that, there's this pandemic.
sentences.zh: 而且最重要的是，还有这场大流行病。

sentences.en: You know, we're deemed essential workers.
sentences.zh: 我们被视为必要行业工人。

sentences.en: We're made to work, you know, with really not any kind of safety equipment other than, you know, just the normal stuff that we had before.
sentences.zh: 我们被迫工作，除了我们以前就有的那些常规装备外，根本没有任何防护设备。

sentences.en: Showing up for work every day.
sentences.zh: 每天按时上班。

sentences.en: It's this super dangerous job.
sentences.zh: 这是一份极其危险的工作。

sentences.en: Every time they go down in that mine, these workers risk their lives.
sentences.zh: 每次下井，这些工人都冒着生命危险。

sentences.en: That's that's just coal mining pandemic or otherwise.
sentences.zh: 无论是否有疫情，煤矿开采就是这样。

sentences.en: You know, we were just a another person in a turnover workforce that had no say or opinion about the job or the work we were doing.
sentences.zh: 我们只是流动劳动力中的一员，对工作本身没有任何发言权或意见。

sentences.en: To feel like the company had made a promise that they were now reneging on.
sentences.zh: 感觉公司违背了当初的承诺。

sentences.en: These workers could not stomach that.
sentences.zh: 这些工人们无法忍受这一点。

sentences.en: And they felt like they had really been betrayed by their employer.
sentences.zh: 他们觉得真的被雇主背叛了。

sentences.en: I guess you just really have to been there and be treated the way we were treated.
sentences.zh: 我想你必须身临其境，经历我们所受的待遇才能明白。

sentences.en: And to see that, you know, how tired that we were, you know, working these long hours, you know, sometimes seven days a week,
sentences.zh: 看到我们有多疲惫，长时间工作，有时一周七天，

sentences.en: you know, 28, 30 days in a row without a day off.
sentences.zh: 连续28、30天没有休息日。

sentences.en: You know, tired of not seeing your family.
sentences.zh: 厌倦了见不到家人。

sentences.en: We had voiced our concerns for the for four years.
sentences.zh: 我们已经表达了四年的担忧。

sentences.en: And it was a kind of a, you know, agreement that, you know, hey, you know, we're ready for a change.
sentences.zh: 大家达成了一种共识，就是我们准备好迎接改变了。

sentences.en: You know, this just ain't working out.
sentences.zh: 这根本行不通。

sentences.en: You know, something's got to give.
sentences.zh: 总得做出点改变。

sentences.en: So that's why on April 1st, 2021, the coal miners decided to go on strike.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是为什么在2021年4月1日，煤矿工人们决定罢工。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.zh: 大家好，我是安德鲁·罗斯·索尔金。

sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日通讯《Dealbook》报道商业和政策新闻。

sentences.en: So, Michael, what has this strike been like day to day?
sentences.zh: 那么，迈克尔，这次罢工的日常情况是怎样的？

sentences.en: Well, let me set the scene.
sentences.zh: 好吧，让我来描述一下当时的场景。

sentences.en: Yeah, the first couple of weeks, it was pretty chaotic.
sentences.zh: 最初的几周非常混乱。

sentences.en: This mine in Brookwood, Alabama is sprawling.
sentences.zh: 这个位于阿拉巴马州布鲁克伍德的矿区非常广阔。

sentences.en: I mean, it goes on for hundreds of miles underground, and there are many, many entrances.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它在地下延伸了数百英里，而且有很多很多入口。

sentences.en: So, at each location, you know, you had 10 to 15 people walking with signs that said, no contract, no coal.
sentences.zh: 所以，在每个地点，都有10到15个人举着写有“没有合同，就没有煤炭”的标语牌。

sentences.en: And what this union did was to set up picket lines at every single entrance.
sentences.zh: 工会所做的就是在每一个入口处都设置了纠察线。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: We had 13 picket lines going.
sentences.zh: 我们当时有13条纠察线。

sentences.en: If you took the time to drive, you know, from one and visit all 13 picket lines, it was 120 miles.
sentences.zh: 如果你花时间开车，从一头到另一头走遍所有13条纠察线，全程有120英里。

sentences.en: I mean, they just flooded this place.
sentences.zh: 他们简直是把这个地方淹没了。

sentences.en: And when the replacement workers showed up, the union workers let them know what they thought of it.
sentences.zh: 当替补工人出现时，工会工人让他们知道了自己的想法。

sentences.en: You'd see them, you know, holler at the scab, call them a scab, maybe a few other words.
sentences.zh: 你会看到他们对着工贼大喊大叫，叫他们工贼，可能还会骂几句别的。

sentences.en: And things got rowdy.
sentences.zh: 场面变得很粗暴。

sentences.en: There was a lot of anger toward them.
sentences.zh: 大家对他们充满了愤怒。

sentences.en: Things got a little violent.
sentences.zh: 情况变得有点暴力了。

sentences.en: There was a few instances, you know, where things kind of got out of hand a little bit.
sentences.zh: 有几次，事情有点失控了。

sentences.en: You know, maybe blocking the roads, you know, maybe slapping a few cars here and there as they go by, you know, shaking them a little bit.
sentences.zh: 比如封锁道路，或者在他们经过时拍打几辆车，摇晃它们之类的。

sentences.en: A busted window or two.
sentences.zh: 打碎了一两扇窗户。

sentences.en: That probably shouldn't have happened.
sentences.zh: 那可能是不该发生的。

sentences.en: So, it was pretty ugly.
sentences.zh: 所以，场面相当难看。

sentences.en: So, day after day at the strike, there's this scene of unionized workers standing at all the entrances, confronting the replacement workers.
sentences.zh: 罢工期间，每天都有工会工人站在所有入口处，与替补工人对峙的场景。

sentences.en: And that goes on for weeks and months.
sentences.zh: 这种情况持续了数周甚至数月。

sentences.en: What you didn't see were political leaders standing arm-in-arm with these unionized coal miners.
sentences.zh: 你没看到的是政治领袖与这些工会煤矿工人站在一起。

sentences.en: Our governor was standing with the company.
sentences.zh: 我们的州长站在公司那边。

sentences.en: For instance, the state police who were under the control of the Republican governor, Kay Ivey.
sentences.zh: 例如，受共和党州长凯·艾维控制的州警察。

sentences.en: Kay Ivey.
sentences.zh: 凯·艾维。

sentences.en: They were ostensibly sent in to keep the peace at the picket line.
sentences.zh: 他们表面上是被派去维持纠察线秩序的。

sentences.en: Blankly supporting the company.
sentences.zh: 实际上是在支持公司。

sentences.en: But the miners say the police seem more intent on helping protect the replacement workers and to harass the union picketers than to stay neutral.
sentences.zh: 但矿工们说，警察似乎更热衷于保护替补工人并骚扰工会纠察队员，而不是保持中立。

sentences.en: And the judge took the side of the company.
sentences.zh: 法官也站在了公司一边。

sentences.en: Then there was the case of this Republican judge who started placing injunctions on the union after the company complained about the picketing.
sentences.zh: 还有一位共和党法官，在公司抱怨纠察活动后，开始对工会下达禁令。

sentences.en: The injunctions just started getting a little more strict each time.
sentences.zh: 这些禁令一次比一次严格。

sentences.en: And those injunctions really limited what the union could do on the picket line.
sentences.zh: 这些禁令极大地限制了工会在纠察线上的活动。

sentences.en: Like, they went from hundreds of people that could be there to, like, a handful.
sentences.zh: 比如，人数从几百人缩减到寥寥数人。

sentences.en: And it really reduced their presence.
sentences.zh: 这确实削弱了他们的声势。

sentences.en: And then finally, one of their Republican senators, Tommy Tuberville, former football coach, huge Trump acolyte, explicitly said that he won't back the miners.
sentences.zh: 最后，他们的共和党参议员之一，前橄榄球教练、特朗普的忠实追随者汤米·塔伯维尔，明确表示他不会支持矿工。

sentences.en: Why not?
sentences.zh: 为什么不呢？

sentences.en: I think it is inappropriate for Congress to weigh in on labor disputes which are properly being resolved through the judicial system.
sentences.zh: 我认为国会介入劳资纠纷是不合适的，这些纠纷应该通过司法系统妥善解决。

sentences.en: His official line is that, you know, it's not his place or Congress's place to get involved in a private business dispute.
sentences.zh: 他的官方说法是，介入私人商业纠纷不是他或国会的职责。

sentences.en: The miners are incredulous.
sentences.zh: 矿工们感到难以置信。

sentences.en: I mean, these are the Republicans that, just a few years ago, said they had the miners' backs.
sentences.zh: 这些共和党人几年前还说他们支持矿工。

sentences.en: When they say that they support the coal industry, I guess they were telling the truth.
sentences.zh: 当他们说支持煤炭行业时，我想他们说的是实话。

sentences.en: You know, they supported the industry and not the worker.
sentences.zh: 他们支持的是行业，而不是工人。

sentences.en: You know, they supported the company and not the worker.
sentences.zh: 他们支持的是公司，而不是工人。

sentences.en: And we're seeing that more, you know, clear as the strike goes on.
sentences.zh: 随着罢工的持续，这一点看得越来越清楚。

sentences.en: The picture just gets clearer as time goes on.
sentences.zh: 随着时间的推移，情况变得越来越清晰。

sentences.en: Was that a moment and a process where you started thinking differently about Republicans?
sentences.zh: 那是一个让你开始对共和党产生不同看法的时刻和过程吗？

sentences.en: I'd say so, yeah.
sentences.zh: 我想是的。

sentences.en: I mean, just given how Donald Trump and the Republican Party essentially ran on the backs of the aggrieved coal miner in 2016.
sentences.zh: 毕竟，唐纳德·特朗普和共和党在2016年本质上就是靠着受委屈的煤矿工人的支持才上台的。

sentences.en: And here's a group of aggrieved coal miners and they won't even talk to them.
sentences.zh: 这里有一群满腹委屈的煤矿工人，而他们甚至都不愿与这些人对话。

sentences.en: So this feels like a potentially golden opportunity for Democrats to show their support for these workers and start to make up ground after losing the coal mining labor unions to Trump.
sentences.zh: 所以，这感觉像是民主党人展现对这些工人支持、并开始挽回在失去煤矿工会支持给特朗普后所失阵地的绝佳机会。

sentences.en: You'd think so.
sentences.zh: 你可能会这么想。

sentences.en: You know, Bernie Sanders has showed us, you know, a good bit of support.
sentences.zh: 你知道，伯尼·桑德斯确实向我们展示了相当多的支持。

sentences.en: But, you know, I guess he's more of an independent.
sentences.zh: 但我想，他更多是以独立人士的身份。

sentences.en: Now, there have been some Democrats and independent Bernie Sanders who have talked about this strike and have criticized the company.
sentences.zh: 目前，确实有一些民主党人和独立人士伯尼·桑德斯谈论过这次罢工，并批评了这家公司。

sentences.en: But it's no one near the attention has been paid by Democrats to this strike that you might expect them to do, given the issues that these workers are raising.
sentences.zh: 但考虑到这些工人提出的问题，民主党人对这次罢工的关注程度远未达到你所预期的水平。

sentences.en: Thousands of Amazon warehouse workers in Alabama will vote on whether to become the company's first unionized facility.
sentences.zh: 阿拉巴马州数千名亚马逊仓库工人将投票决定是否成立该公司首个工会设施。

sentences.en: What's even more striking to coal miners like Braxton is how Democrats reacted to a union effort going on just 30 miles away in Bessemer at an Amazon warehouse.
sentences.zh: 对于像布拉克斯顿这样的煤矿工人来说，更令人震惊的是，民主党人对距离这里仅30英里外贝塞默亚马逊仓库正在进行的工会运动作出了怎样的反应。

sentences.en: I am welcome today to have a delegation from Congress who are standing with these workers.
sentences.zh: 今天我很高兴有一位国会代表团成员与这些工人站在一起。

sentences.en: There's a congressional delegation that came to the facility and held a press conference.
sentences.zh: 有一个国会代表团来到该设施并举行了新闻发布会。

sentences.en: We hear you, Alabama workers, and we are with you.
sentences.zh: 阿拉巴马的工人们，我们听到了你们的声音，我们与你们同在。

sentences.en: There should be no intimidation, no coercion, no threats, no anti-union propaganda.
sentences.zh: 不应有恐吓、胁迫、威胁或反工会宣传。

sentences.en: President Biden weighed in, warning the company not to mess with the unionization vote.
sentences.zh: 拜登总统介入了此事，警告该公司不要干预工会投票。

sentences.en: And it's your right, not that of an employer.
sentences.zh: 这是你们的权利，而不是雇主的权利。

sentences.en: It's your right.
sentences.zh: 这是你们的权利。

sentences.en: No employer can take that right away.
sentences.zh: 任何雇主都不能剥夺这一权利。

sentences.en: So make your voice heard.
sentences.zh: 所以，发出你们的声音吧。

sentences.en: Which is almost unheard of for a sitting president to directly weigh in on a unionization effort.
sentences.zh: 对于一位在任总统来说，直接介入工会运动几乎是闻所未闻的。

sentences.en: I mean, the Democrats made supporting those Amazon workers a big moment.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，民主党人将支持那些亚马逊工人视为一个重大时刻。

sentences.en: These Democrats or the Democratic Party, the core of it has always aligned itself with workers, and particularly unionized workers.
sentences.zh: 这些民主党人或民主党，其核心一直与工人，特别是工会工人保持一致。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So is that doubly frustrating or?
sentences.zh: 所以这是否让人感到加倍沮丧？

sentences.en: It really is.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: I guess being the industry that we're in, you know, a lot of them don't want to get involved.
sentences.zh: 我想因为我们所处的行业，你知道，他们很多人不想卷入其中。

sentences.en: Almost to the point where we've been abandoned by both sides, you know, really.
sentences.zh: 几乎到了我们被双方抛弃的地步，真的。

sentences.en: With our strike, we have.
sentences.zh: 就我们的罢工而言，确实如此。

sentences.en: I mean, we have been abandoned by both sides.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们被双方都抛弃了。

sentences.en: Do you feel like, you know, for the Democrats, do you understand that dilemma or do you feel that that is misguided?
sentences.zh: 你觉得，对于民主党人来说，你理解那种困境吗？还是你觉得那是误导？

sentences.en: I think it's misguided.
sentences.zh: 我认为那是误导。

sentences.en: You know, each party picks two main things, you know, to Democrats is fossil fuels and abortion.
sentences.zh: 你知道，每个党派都会挑选两件主要的事情，对民主党来说是化石燃料和堕胎。

sentences.en: And then Republicans, their big argument is more pro-fossil fuels, you know, pro-gun and anti-abortion.
sentences.zh: 而共和党，他们的大论点更多是支持化石燃料、支持拥枪和反对堕胎。

sentences.en: It's like the both sides are so worried about these three items that they've lost focus on everything else.
sentences.zh: 感觉双方都太担心这三件事，以至于忽略了其他一切。

sentences.en: So a coal miner like Braxton and his co-workers are in a very strange position.
sentences.zh: 所以像布拉克斯顿和他的同事这样的煤矿工人处于一个非常奇怪的境地。

sentences.en: They were once a group beloved by Democrats, and then they were won over by Republicans.
sentences.zh: 他们曾经是民主党人钟爱的群体，后来又被共和党人赢得了支持。

sentences.en: And now in their greatest moment of need, if you're someone like Braxton, you wake up and you realize neither party is your ally.
sentences.zh: 而现在，在他们最需要帮助的时候，如果你是布拉克斯顿这样的人，你会醒悟过来，意识到没有哪一方是你的盟友。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And without any political support, the strike is dragging on and on.
sentences.zh: 由于没有任何政治支持，罢工一直在拖延。

sentences.en: It's about a year since the strike began, and Braxton needs a job.
sentences.zh: 罢工开始已经快一年了，布拉克斯顿需要一份工作。

sentences.en: You know, I kind of applaud to Amazon as a joke, almoSt.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我几乎是开玩笑地向亚马逊投了简历。

sentences.en: Ironically, he actually gets a job at the Amazon warehouse in Bessemer that he's been trying to unionize.
sentences.zh: 讽刺的是，他竟然真的在贝塞默的亚马逊仓库得到了一份工作，而他一直试图在那里组织工会。

sentences.en: This is the same warehouse, right, where the now-failed unionization efforts happened and where Democratic officials came out to show their support.
sentences.zh: 这就是同一个仓库，对吧？那个现在已经失败的工会化努力发生的地方，也是民主党官员出来表示支持的地方。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So I go in through their cattle herding process of being hired and, you know, start.
sentences.zh: 所以我经历了他们那种像赶牛一样的招聘流程，然后就开始工作了。

sentences.en: I go through my three days training for the first three days, and then on the next week, you know,
sentences.zh: 我完成了前三天的培训，然后在接下来的一周，你知道，

sentences.en: I come into Amazon wearing my camo union shirt, and everybody's kind of looking at me funny.
sentences.zh: 我穿着我的迷彩工会衬衫走进亚马逊，每个人都用奇怪的眼光看着我。

sentences.en: I mean, your camo uniform, that's like a union colors.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你的迷彩制服，那就像是工会的颜色。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And while he's there working, sorting boxes, working the overnight shift, he himself gets involved in the effort to unionize at the Bessemer warehouse.
sentences.zh: 当他在那里工作、分拣包裹、上夜班时，他自己也参与了贝塞默仓库的工会组织工作。

sentences.en: Well, I mean, you know, a lot of them, you know, were curious, you know, you know, why did you go on strike?
sentences.zh: 嗯，我的意思是，你知道，他们很多人，你知道，都很好奇，你知道，你为什么要罢工？

sentences.en: You know, you were already making, you know, this amount, you know, and we kind of explained to them, you know, it wasn't necessarily about the money.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你已经赚了，你知道，这么多钱，你知道，我们向他们解释了，你知道，这不一定是为了钱。

sentences.en: You know, a lot of it was the lack of respect that we used to have.
sentences.zh: 你知道，很大程度上是因为我们曾经拥有的那种尊重的缺失。

sentences.en: What was the biggest thing you've told them, the biggest, you know, reason they should join a union?
sentences.zh: 你告诉他们最重要的事情是什么？他们应该加入工会的最大理由是什么？

sentences.en: What's the main thing you tell them?
sentences.zh: 你告诉他们的核心是什么？

sentences.en: The solidarity.
sentences.zh: 团结。

sentences.en: I mean, me just telling them, you know, hey, you need a union because it could do this better for you, this better for you.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我只是告诉他们，嘿，你需要一个工会，因为它能为你做得更好，为你做得更好。

sentences.en: And then me showing them, you know, what the union has been able to do.
sentences.zh: 然后我向他们展示，你知道，工会已经能够做到什么。

sentences.en: And say, right now, you're only one voice at a time.
sentences.zh: 并说，现在，你一次只能发出一个声音。

sentences.en: If you were a union and you were having the problem, you know, you have, you know, six million instead of one.
sentences.zh: 如果你是一个工会，当你遇到问题时，你知道，你有六百万人，而不是一个人。

sentences.en: You don't just have, you know, yourself trying to fight a battle.
sentences.zh: 你不仅仅是，你知道，你自己试图去打一场仗。

sentences.en: You have an army of millions, you know, that are ready to support you in your fight.
sentences.zh: 你拥有一支数百万人的军队，你知道，他们准备在你的战斗中支持你。

sentences.en: I mean, if it wasn't for the solidarity of just the working class that, you know, we wouldn't have been able to last this long.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果不是因为工人阶级的团结，你知道，我们不可能坚持这么久。

sentences.en: You know, when we put always sort of labels or, you know, how we identify Democrat, Republican,
sentences.zh: 你知道，当我们总是贴上标签，或者，你知道，我们如何定义民主党人、共和党人，

sentences.en: do you identify most primarily as a union worker?
sentences.zh: 你最主要将自己定义为工会工人吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, that's what, you know, I consider myself a union worker.
sentences.zh: 是的，我的意思是，这就是，你知道，我认为自己是一名工会工人。

sentences.en: You know, that's what I am.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我就是这样的人。

sentences.en: And if possible, that's what I'm going to stay.
sentences.zh: 如果可能的话，我打算一直保持这样。

sentences.en: So where does that leave you politically?
sentences.zh: 那么这让你在政治上处于什么位置？

sentences.en: Ah, kind of in the middle of the road.
sentences.zh: 啊，算是处于中间地带吧。

sentences.en: You know, we've had a lot of support from, you know, local and state, you know, DSA chapters.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们得到了很多来自，你知道，地方和州，你知道，美国民主社会主义者（DSA）分会的支持。

sentences.en: You know, the Birmingham DSA chapter shows tremendous support for us.
sentences.zh: 你知道，伯明翰DSA分会给予了我们巨大的支持。

sentences.en: What's that, DSA?
sentences.zh: 那是什么，DSA？

sentences.en: The Democratic Socialists of America.
sentences.zh: 美国民主社会主义者。

sentences.en: They're very pro-worker, you know, I mean, they support workers.
sentences.zh: 他们非常支持工人，你知道，我的意思是，他们支持工人。

sentences.en: It doesn't matter the industry.
sentences.zh: 这与行业无关。

sentences.en: You know, to them, we're still a worker, you know.
sentences.zh: 你知道，对他们来说，我们仍然是工人，你知道。

sentences.en: Yeah, we work in fossil fuel, but at the end of the day, we're still a worker.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们在化石燃料行业工作，但归根结底，我们仍然是工人。

sentences.en: That is important, you know, as a worker in another industry.
sentences.zh: 这很重要，你知道，作为另一个行业的工人。

sentences.en: Do you feel like that as a worker, as a coal miner, that there's no place for you in the mainstream political conversation right now?
sentences.zh: 你是否觉得作为一名工人，作为一名煤矿工人，现在主流政治对话中没有你的位置？

sentences.en: Yeah, pretty much.
sentences.zh: 是的，差不多吧。

sentences.en: I mean, each election year, each party stands up and says, you know, we're going to do this and we're going to do that.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，每到选举年，每个党派都会站出来说，你知道，我们要这样做，我们要那样做。

sentences.en: But, and then at the end of the four years, you know, it's very rare that we've seen, you know, anything happen that they promised would happen at the beginning of their time.
sentences.zh: 但是，在四年结束时，你知道，我们很少看到，你知道，他们在任期开始时承诺的事情有任何实现。

sentences.en: I'd like to actually see from either side just, you know, a change toward the workers of the country.
sentences.zh: 我实际上希望看到任何一方，你知道，朝着这个国家的工人做出改变。

sentences.en: I mean, just me as a, you know, average working class American, I can't see where either side has done anything to help the working class.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，作为一个，你知道，普通的美国工人阶级，我看不出哪一方做了任何事情来帮助工人阶级。

sentences.en: So, Michael, I wonder how we should think about Braxton's story.
sentences.zh: 所以，迈克尔，我想知道我们应该如何看待布拉克斯顿的故事。

sentences.en: Is this the story of a very unique set of circumstances, a dying industry coal that has gotten caught between the changing identities of the two parties?
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常独特的情况的故事吗？一个垂死的行业——煤炭，被夹在两个党派不断变化的身份认同之间？

sentences.en: Or is this a story that we should think about differently?
sentences.zh: 还是说这是一个我们应该以不同方式思考的故事？

sentences.en: Is it a measure of just how much both parties have failed to speak to working people like Braxton?
sentences.zh: 这是否衡量了两个党派在为像布拉克斯顿这样的劳动人民发声方面失败到了什么程度？

sentences.en: How do you think about that?
sentences.zh: 你是怎么想的？

sentences.en: So, Braxton's one worker in Alabama at a coal mine.
sentences.zh: 所以，布拉克斯顿是阿拉巴马州煤矿的一名工人。

sentences.en: But when you think of what a worker like him means for politics, national politics, and the politics of the working class, someone like Braxton,
sentences.zh: 但当你想到像他这样的工人对政治、国家政治以及工人阶级政治意味着什么时，像布拉克斯顿这样的人，

sentences.en: who's had this remarkable journey politically, he should be paid attention to.
sentences.zh: 他在政治上经历了如此非凡的旅程，他应该受到关注。

sentences.en: I told you over and over, it is my belief, if you don't ever quit a fight, I don't care where that fight is, you cannot lose that fight.
sentences.zh: 我一遍又一遍地告诉过你，这是我的信念，如果你从不放弃一场战斗，我不在乎那场战斗在哪里，你就不会输掉那场战斗。

sentences.en: I had this experience when I was in Alabama reporting this story, and I was at a rally at the Union Hall, and I looked out at the crowd.
sentences.zh: 我在阿拉巴马州报道这个故事时有过这种经历，当时我在工会大厅参加集会，我看着人群。

sentences.en: And I was just struck by how diverse it was, and how many different types of people there were, black, white, women, men.
sentences.zh: 我被它的多样性所震撼，有这么多不同类型的人，黑人、白人、女性、男性。

sentences.en: And I thought, wow, like, these people have this one thing in common, which is that they are sticking with this fight.
sentences.zh: 我想，哇，这些人有一个共同点，那就是他们坚持这场战斗。

sentences.en: And I thought, that is something really remarkable.
sentences.zh: 我想，那真是非凡的事情。

sentences.en: Yeah, we're going to win this fight, and I believe we're going to win it sooner than you might think.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们要赢得这场战斗，我相信我们会比你想象的更快赢得它。

sentences.en: I talked to workers all over the place.
sentences.zh: 我和各地的人交谈过。

sentences.en: Workers who are in unions, who are not in unions.
sentences.zh: 那些在工会里的工人，那些不在工会里的工人。

sentences.en: They work in manufacturing plants.
sentences.zh: 他们在制造工厂工作。

sentences.en: They work in Walmart, Dollar General.
sentences.zh: 他们在沃尔玛、美元店工作。

sentences.en: And their stories are very similar.
sentences.zh: 他们的故事非常相似。

sentences.en: There seems to be this grand bargain that's been broken.
sentences.zh: 似乎有一个伟大的契约被打破了。

sentences.en: There was this notion in this country that you get a job, you show up on time, you do well, you can be respected by your employer, you can be paid fairly, and you can advance.
sentences.zh: 在这个国家有一种观念，你找一份工作，准时上班，表现出色，你就能得到雇主的尊重，你能得到公平的报酬，你就能获得晋升。

sentences.en: And that doesn't seem to be working right now.
sentences.zh: 而现在这似乎行不通了。

sentences.en: There's a whole bunch of people over in that building that hate us.
sentences.zh: 那栋大楼里有一大群人讨厌我们。

sentences.en: They just hate us because we won't bow down.
sentences.zh: 他们就是讨厌我们，因为我们不愿屈服。

sentences.en: Because we won't say, yes, do whatever you want to us.
sentences.zh: 因为我们不会说，好的，随你们怎么对待我们吧。

sentences.en: We won't do that.
sentences.zh: 我们不会那样做。

sentences.en: And they don't understand that we will not subject ourselves to their mercy.
sentences.zh: 他们不明白，我们不会让自己任由他们摆布。

sentences.en: I want to thank you for standing up and surviving this long.
sentences.zh: 我要感谢你们站出来并坚持了这么久。

sentences.en: I want you to know, this is close enough that I can feel it.
sentences.zh: 我想让你们知道，这已经足够近了，我能感觉到。

sentences.en: This is close enough that I can taste it.
sentences.zh: 这已经足够近了，我能尝到它的滋味。

sentences.en: And all we need to do is be stronger than them.
sentences.zh: 我们所要做的就是比他们更强大。

sentences.en: One day longer than them.
sentences.zh: 比他们多坚持一天。

sentences.en: One day stronger than them.
sentences.zh: 比他们强大一天。

sentences.en: God bless all of you.
sentences.zh: 上帝保佑你们所有人。

sentences.en: You will!
sentences.zh: 你们会赢的！

sentences.en: Oh, Michael, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 哦，迈克尔，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 纽约时报应用程序？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 解锁了？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to the Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 每个人都知道你需要订阅《时报》才能访问所有的报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore the Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果你能免费探索《时报》一个月，而无需输入信用卡信息呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download the New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你第一次下载《纽约时报》应用程序时，你在应用程序中的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 用一个月的时间越过付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to the New York Times, download the Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅《纽约时报》，今天就下载《时报》应用程序，获得30天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要知道的其他事情。

sentences.en: Over the weekend, the daughter of a top advisor to Vladimir Putin was killed in what appeared to be a car bombing inside Russia.
sentences.zh: 周末，弗拉基米尔·普京的一位高级顾问的女儿在俄罗斯境内发生的一起疑似汽车炸弹袭击中丧生。

sentences.en: The woman's death is poised to be a new flashpoint in Russia's war with Ukraine because the victim's father, Alexander Dugin,
sentences.zh: 这位女性的死亡可能会成为俄罗斯与乌克兰战争中的一个新冲突点，因为受害者的父亲亚历山大·杜金，

sentences.en: helped shape the ideas behind Russia's invasion and is an outspoken advocate of the war.
sentences.zh: 帮助塑造了俄罗斯入侵背后的思想，并且是这场战争的直言不讳的倡导者。

sentences.en: Ukrainian officials adamantly denied any rule in her death and said it could be the result of an internal Russian dispute.
sentences.zh: 乌克兰官员坚决否认与她的死亡有任何关系，并表示这可能是俄罗斯内部纠纷的结果。

sentences.en: It was unclear whether it was Dugin or his daughter who was the intended target of the blaSt.
sentences.zh: 目前尚不清楚爆炸的目标是杜金本人还是他的女儿。

sentences.en: I certainly hope that if it was an attack on either one of those people, that it was an internal Russian affair and it wasn't something emanating from Ukraine.
sentences.zh: 我当然希望如果这是针对这两个人中任何一个人的袭击，那也是俄罗斯内部的事务，而不是源自乌克兰的事情。

sentences.en: In an interview on Sunday with CNN, Congressman Adam Schiff, the chairman of the House Intelligence Committee, said he hoped that Ukraine was not involved.
sentences.zh: 在周日接受CNN采访时，众议院情报委员会主席亚当·希夫众议员表示，他希望乌克兰没有参与其中。

sentences.en: We have seen terrible war crimes by Russia against Ukraine, and Russia should be held accountable.
sentences.zh: 我们已经看到了俄罗斯对乌克兰犯下的可怕战争罪行，俄罗斯应该被追究责任。

sentences.en: And I certainly would never want to see anything like an attack on civilians by Ukraine and hope that their representations are correct.
sentences.zh: 我当然永远不希望看到乌克兰对平民发动任何形式的袭击，并希望他们的陈述是正确的。

sentences.zh: 今天的节目由戴安娜·阮、埃里克·克鲁普克和琳赛·加里森制作。

sentences.en: It was edited by Mark George, contains original music by Marion Lozano and Chelsea Daniel, and was engineered by Marion Lozano.
sentences.zh: 由马克·乔治编辑，包含玛丽昂·洛萨诺和切尔西·丹尼尔的原创音乐，并由玛丽昂·洛萨诺进行工程制作。

sentences.zh: 我们的主题音乐由Wonderly的吉姆·布伦伯格和本·兰兹伯格创作。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这就是《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine, until this summer, when elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直作为一个受到严格控制的机器运作，直到今年夏天，选举迎来了一群自称改革者的人。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那时起，该党一直处于一场残酷、混乱且有时令人兴奋的斗争之中。
